steps.title: Fixed, licensed test sets
steps.text: Every test image is public-licence (Pexels, GB82, libjpeg-turbo, F-Droid screenshots, Kenney pixel art and OpenMoji icons) with its origin and licence recorded in the repository manifest. The initial 100,000-trial sweep used 50 images (30 PNG, 20 JPEG); the SSIMULACRA2 validation pool expanded to 65 real PNGs and 23 JPEGs; and the head-to-head ImageOptim comparison uses 8 files (4 PNG, 4 JPEG).

steps.title: Recipe sweep
steps.text: In the initial sweep, each of the 50 images ran through 2,000 recipes for its format. PNG recipes combined palette quantisation (pngquant), OxiPNG and Zopfli in different orders and settings; JPEG recipes varied MozJPEG quality, scan mode and lossless Huffman recompression. Every trial recorded size, time, pixel exactness, SSIM and PSNR and can be replayed from the saved plan.

steps.title: Two quality checks
steps.text: The goal is the smallest file that still looks right at three levels: Visually lossless (invisible even zoomed in), High quality (looks identical at normal viewing size) and Good for web (crisp for web pages). The 100k sweep used fast SSIM floors (0.995, 0.98, 0.95) to map out recipe chains. Because SSIM is forgiving near the top, finalists and the shipped Smart engine are gated on SSIMULACRA2 (floors 90, 80 and 70), with an alpha-aware check over black, white and grey backgrounds for transparent images.

steps.title: Effort tiers
steps.text: Effort is encode time relative to the fastest recipes on the same image, so image size does not skew it. Fast allows up to 3× the fastest recipe, Balanced up to 15×, and Thorough has no cap. Real times are reported in seconds per megapixel (a 1000×1000 image; multiply by 8–12 for a typical phone photo).

steps.title: Honest scoring
steps.text: Picking a recipe on an image and scoring it on the same image flatters it. Champion recipes are therefore scored leave-one-source-out: chosen on all other images, then applied to the held-out image. Splits are always by source image, never by trial.

steps.title: Redundancy and chain alerts
steps.text: Recipes that produce byte-identical output are counted as duplicates, and recipes within 1% size and 0.002 SSIM on ≥95% of images are collapsed to the fastest one. Comparing each chain against its shorter prefix (such as OxiPNG vs. OxiPNG + Zopfli) drives the Architect editor's warnings about steps that add time without saving bytes.

steps.title: Head-to-head comparison
steps.text: The real ImageOptim app (with its installed preferences recorded) is compared on the same 8 files against NEO's matching recipes, NEO Smart in the same format (cjpegli for JPEG, quantette-wasm + OxiPNG for PNG), and NEO Smart with automatic format choice (racing PNG, JPEG, WebP, JPEG XL and AVIF).

limits: The 100,000-trial sweep on Overview, Rankings and Explore is complete (50 images: 30 PNG, 20 JPEG) and gated on SSIM. See the SSIMULACRA2 page for the stricter perceptual re-check.
50 sweep images (and 65 real PNGs / 23 JPEGs in the validation pool) is still modest; content types with only 1–3 images are marked as indicative.
Times were measured on one Apple Silicon Mac with two workers running at once and include start-up overhead; your hardware will differ.
The head-to-head ImageOptim comparison uses 8 files (4 PNG, 4 JPEG) and one installed ImageOptim preference set.

sources.name: Google Gemini consultation
sources.took: Group train and test splits by source image; run a Pareto analysis before any modelling; prefer a target-quality search to fixed recipes; avoid testing many recipes on few images.
sources.folded: Leave-one-source-out scoring, champion sets, and the second-phase plan. Its cited resources were each checked independently, below.
sources.caveat: Two of its citations could not be confirmed (see Not found). Its advice to train LightGBM with 18 to 50 sources was judged premature.

sources.name: SPCP, Still Picture Coding Performance (Fukushima et al., PCS 2025)
sources.took: A large public benchmark of ten photo codecs with many quality metrics, including SSIMULACRA2 and Butteraugli.
sources.folded: Used as a sanity reference for JPEG, WebP and AVIF behaviour and for choosing metrics. Planned: compare our MozJPEG curves on shared images to catch harness errors.
sources.caveat: No PNG, palette or lossless modes and no licence stated, so it cannot replace our PNG data.

sources.name: Cleanor Storage Lab
sources.took: Small CC BY 4.0 dataset of JPEG, WebP and AVIF size at SSIM and PSNR on Kodak and phone photos.
sources.caveat: Small, photographic, and unrelated to our PNG recompression chains.

sources.name: SSIMULACRA2 (Cloudinary)
sources.took: Score bands (50 medium, 70 high, 80 very high, 90 visually lossless) and published correlation with human ratings (about 0.89 on the independent CID22 validation set).
sources.folded: Defines the planned SSIMULACRA2 tiers for re-scoring. We run the Rust port ssimulacra2_rs 0.5.2 and record versions, since score scales differ between releases.
sources.caveat: Cloudinary authored both the metric and the CID22 dataset. No source we found validates it for banding, text or alpha.

sources.name: CID22 dataset (Cloudinary)
sources.took: About 22,000 images with subjective scores across a MozJPEG-like quality range.
sources.folded: Planned: calibrate the score thresholds for JPEG without running our own human study.

sources.name: Jpegli rater study (Google)
sources.took: Equal quality at about 28% lower bitrate than libjpeg-turbo in an 18-rater study.
sources.folded: Implemented via cjpegli in NEO Smart mode (CLI, MCP and desktop), where it saves 3–13% more than MozJPEG at equal SSIMULACRA2.
sources.caveat: Run by the encoder's authors; we verified gains independently on our own corpus.

sources.name: pngquant and libimagequant documentation
sources.took: Median-cut palettes with refinement, premultiplied alpha, adaptive dithering, the dither, posterize and speed options, and the 5% quality cost of speed 10.
sources.folded: Informs the dither, posterize and speed experiments and the explanation of why recipe order and quality limits matter.
sources.caveat: Documents what the tool does, not how it compares with other quantisers.

sources.name: OxiPNG README
sources.took: Levels 0 to 6 with diminishing returns, and the alpha option that changes invisible pixels.
sources.folded: Explains why OxiPNG levels barely matter in our sweep and motivates the alpha-handling experiment.

sources.name: ImageOptim source and bundled tools
sources.took: The exact tool order and flags the app uses: pngquant, OxiPNG, advpng and others for PNG; jpegtran plus jpegoptim with a quality cap for JPEG.
sources.folded: Basis of the parity table and the north-star comparison; it exposed that NEO's lossy JPEG recipe re-encodes with MozJPEG while the app caps quality.
sources.caveat: The app's behaviour depends on the user's preferences, which are recorded with every comparison.

sources.name: libwebp near-lossless post (2015)
sources.took: Estimated extra savings from near-lossless, from 5 to 10% at level 80 to 40 to 50% at 20 or below.
sources.folded: Candidate for the later format experiments.
sources.caveat: Dated and a developer's estimate; to be re-measured, not quoted.

sources.name: imgmin and target-quality search
sources.took: Binary search of a quality knob to hit an error target is established practice.
sources.folded: Basis of the planned per-image target-quality search as the competitor to a recipe classifier.
sources.caveat: Its error metric is simple; we would use SSIM, then SSIMULACRA2.

sources.name: Per-title encoding (Netflix) and Hyperband
sources.took: Keep the convex hull of a bytes versus quality grid; use successive halving to prune search spaces.
sources.folded: Our per-image frontier is the image analogue; successive halving is planned for the second sweep.
sources.caveat: No published application to image codecs was found.

sources.name: Video pre-filter studies (for example Bilibili RPP)
sources.took: Perceptual pre-filtering saved roughly 13 to 19% bitrate in video.
sources.folded: Treated as a reason to test pre-blur and denoise, not as evidence they help still images.
sources.caveat: Video, not JPEG or PNG. We found no still-image study of blur before encoding.

notfound.name: nucliweb/compare-codecs-action
notfound.note: Cited by the Gemini consultation. We could not find it; treated as unverified. The idea (binary search to a target SSIMULACRA2) is sound and is being built directly.

notfound.name: Jake Archibald 2026 codec comparisons
notfound.note: Cited by the Gemini consultation. Not opened or verified; not used.

notfound.name: Wu versus NeuQuant versus libimagequant
notfound.note: Only forum comments were found, no head-to-head benchmark. This is an experiment to run, not a result.

notfound.name: oxipng and friends comparison (2025)
notfound.note: The page exists but its numbers could not be retrieved, so it is not used until read in full.

metrics.name: SSIMULACRA2
metrics.note: Primary human-vision score used by NEO Smart mode (0–100). 90 = visually lossless (invisible even zoomed in); 80 = high quality (identical at normal size); 70 = good for web.

metrics.name: Butteraugli
metrics.note: Spots localized flaws like colour banding, ringing around sharp edges and JPEG blocking. Used as a second check on finalists.

metrics.name: DSSIM
metrics.note: Perceptual structural difference score; used as an independent cross-check alongside SSIMULACRA2.

metrics.name: NEO SSIM and PSNR
metrics.note: Fast similarity score used across all 100,000 sweep trials. Useful for ranking recipe chains, but too forgiving near the top to be the final quality gate.

metrics.name: CVVDP (ColorVideoVDP)
metrics.note: Display-aware vision model (JOD scale, 10 = identical) recorded on north-star benchmarks as an extra sanity check.

metrics.name: zensim and iqa (Rust crates)
metrics.note: Potential faster Rust scorers for future large sweeps; to be calibrated against SSIMULACRA2 first.

metrics.name: LPIPS, DISTS and VMAF
metrics.note: Neural or video-trained metrics; less reliable for still graphics, UI text and transparent edges.

metrics.name: HDR-VDP-3, FLIP, MS-SSIM
metrics.note: HDR-VDP and FLIP target HDR/3D rendering; MS-SSIM correlates worse with human ratings than SSIMULACRA2.
